{{use dmy dates|date=November 2021}}

'''Glenn Mitchell Wightman''' {{post-nominals|country=AUS|PSM}} (born 1961)<ref>{{Cite web|title=Wightman, Glenn M. (Glenn Mitchell) (1961–)|url=https://trove.nla.gov.au/people/551411|access-date=2021-11-07|website=trove.nla.gov.au|archive-date=6 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211106203321/https://trove.nla.gov.au/people/551411|url-status=live}}</ref> is an ethnobotanist working for the Department of Environment Parks and Water Security,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Department of Environment Parks and Water Security|url=https://www.gbif.org/grscicoll/institution/6d5fac5e-78e7-4425-b886-ee1e072b92f3|access-date=2021-11-07|website=www.gbif.org|language=en|archive-date=7 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211107214706/https://www.gbif.org/grscicoll/institution/6d5fac5e-78e7-4425-b886-ee1e072b92f3|url-status=live}}</ref> in [[Palmerston, Northern Territory|Palmerston]].<ref name=":0" /> He works closely with various aboriginal language groups to document plant and animal names and their usage in the culture.<ref name="one">{{cite Q|Q106088130}}</ref><ref name="two">{{cite Q|Q106088428}}</ref><ref name="tiwi">{{cite Q|Q109442600}}</ref>  In doing so, he has been helping to preserve some 48 Aboriginal languages in collaboration with some 252 Indigenous co-authors.<ref name=":1" />  He has also done biocultural work in [[Indonesia]].<ref>{{Cite Q|Q108329560}}</ref><ref>{{Cite Q|Q108329562}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite Q|Q108329559}}cite Q</ref>

Wightman was born in 1961 at [[Leongatha]], Victoria,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Wightman, Glenn Mitchell – biography|url=https://www.anbg.gov.au/biography/wightman-glenn-mitchell.html|access-date=2021-11-07|website=www.anbg.gov.au|language=en|archive-date=7 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211107212455/https://www.anbg.gov.au/biography/wightman-glenn-mitchell.html|url-status=live}}</ref> and graduated from [[Monash University]] in 1982 with a BSc, majoring in botany and geology.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|date=2019-10-27|title=Bringing Indigenous languages back from the brink|url=https://lens.monash.edu/@monash-life/2019/10/27/1377046?slug=preserving-indigenous-languages|access-date=2021-11-07|website=Monash Lens|language=en-US|archive-date=25 January 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230125065736/https://lens.monash.edu/@monash-life/2019/10/27/1377046?slug=preserving-indigenous-languages|url-status=live}}</ref>

In 2008 he curated ''Replant: A New Generation of Botanical Art'', an exhibition held at the [[Royal Botanic Garden, Sydney|Royal Botanic Gardens]] in Sydney of illustrations of water lilies by six indigenous and non-indigenous artists in collaboration with the [[Nauiyu Nambiyu Community|Nauiyu]] community in the [[Northern Territory]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Skatssoon|first=Judy|date=2008-07-04|title=Water lilies more than pretty flowers|url=https://www.smh.com.au/lifestyle/water-lilies-more-than-pretty-flowers-20080704-31m1.html|access-date=2021-11-07|website=The Sydney Morning Herald|language=en|archive-date=7 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211107213847/https://www.smh.com.au/lifestyle/water-lilies-more-than-pretty-flowers-20080704-31m1.html|url-status=live}}</ref> The exhibition of prints was displayed in the Cowra Regional Art Gallery in central New South Wales in 2011.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2011-10-16|title=New exhibitions – REPLANT: a new generation of botanical art and RACHEL ELLIS: New Works|url=https://cowraartgallery.com.au/new-exhibitions-replant-a-new-generation-of-botanical-art-and-rachel-ellis-new-works|access-date=2021-11-08|website=Cowra Regional Art Gallery|language=en-US|archive-date=8 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211108022215/https://cowraartgallery.com.au/new-exhibitions-replant-a-new-generation-of-botanical-art-and-rachel-ellis-new-works|url-status=live}}</ref>

He has published one plant name: ''[[Atalaya brevialata]]'' Cowie & Wightman.<ref name="Nuytsia">{{cite Q|Q98565598}}</ref>

{{botanist|Wightman|inline=yes}}

== Honours and recognition ==
In the [[2011 Australia Day Honours|Australia Day Honours]] of 2011, he was awarded the [[Public Service Medal (Australia)|Public Service Medal]] for "For outstanding public service to the maintenance of Indigenous languages and culture in the Northern Territory, particularly Indigenous biological knowledge of plants, animals and landscapes".<ref>{{Cite news|date=2011-01-26|title=AUSTRALIA DAY 2011 HONOURS|work=Commonwealth of Australia Gazette. Special|url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article240487638|access-date=2021-11-06}}</ref>

In 2021 he won the Northern Territory's Natural Resource Management's lifetime achievement award.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NT NRM AWARDS |url=https://www.tnrmconference.org.au/nt-nrm-awards-21 |access-date=2022-04-22 |website=TNRM Conference |language=en |archive-date=27 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220527021633/https://www.tnrmconference.org.au/nt-nrm-awards-21 |url-status=live }}</ref>
